mainEntity.name: What can go wrong when AI helps plan or run a webinar?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main risks are inaccurate claims, generic content, hidden bias, privacy exposure, weak audience fit, technical failure, and over-automation. Reduce them with narrow objectives, source checks, permission controls, rehearsal, accessibility testing, and human approval before publishing or spending. Context: AI-assisted meeting tools may transcribe or record voices and images, so organizers should review platform privacy, retention, administrative settings, and attendee disclosures. Key factors: - What participant data is collected - Which accounts AI can access - Whether recordings are retained or reused - Who approves external actions Practical guidance: Share a clear recording and AI-use notice, collect only needed information, and offer an appropriate alternative when possible. Keep credentials secure and test permissions in a non-production setting. Run My AI Biz’s educational model supports human-directed automation rather than unattended decisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: AI can produce false claims, biased examples, poor audience fit, privacy problems, or a polished deck that fails in the live session. Reduce risk with source verification, limited permissions, a recording notice, accessibility checks, technical rehearsal, and human approval before content is published or money is spent.
